title: POC scoping: cost modeling with Arcadia Systems
summary: AE + SE scoped a 6-8 week POC to validate latency SLOs and cost/unit economics for Arcadia's customer-facing summarization feature. Discussed workload (avg tokens in/out, QPS), benchmark plan, beating dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs, batching/cache knobs, and next steps to run a benchmark with a sampled dataset.
next_steps: Jordan to send POC pricing and pilot contract draft by 2025-10-10
Priya to share benchmark runbook and sample scripts by 2025-10-09
Arcadia to provide 1 week of anonymized request traces and 1000 sample prompts by 2025-10-13
action_items: Jordan Lee (AE) - Send POC pricing + pricing sensitivities (hosted vs dedicated) - due 2025-10-10
Priya Sharma (SE) - Share benchmark runbook, load generator, and suggested metrics - due 2025-10-09
Michael Torres (CTO) - Provide anonymized traffic sample and success criteria doc - due 2025-10-13
Liam O'Connor (DevOps) - Confirm internal VPN/VPC details for private pilot (if needed) - due 2025-10-15
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Arcadia CTO), Simone Park (ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (DevOps), Terry Nguyen (Product)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh we wanted to run through the POC scope focused on cost modeling and unit economics for your summarization feature. Are those high level goals still correct, Michael?
00:32 Michael Torres: Yeah that's right, we want to validate two things: 1) can we meet our 95th percentile latency SLO of about 200ms for interactive flows, and 2) what's the expected per-request cost so we can model economics at scale.
01:10 Priya Sharma: Great, and to do that we'll need a sample of your current request distribution — average token in/out, peak QPS, distribution of input lengths. Even a 1 week trace is super helpful.
01:47 Simone Park: We can export logs, yes — average request right now is about 350 tokens in, 600 tokens out for the long summary, but we also have short summaries that are ~120 in/200 out. Peak QPS on weekdays is around 18–22, sustained 10–12.
02:25 Jordan Lee: Perfect, that mix matters a lot for batching savings. Quick framing on cost: for hosted inference we typically model per-1k-token costs; ballpark hosted for a model of this class is around $0.45–0.65 per 1k tokens depending on model variant and caching. Dedicated can get much lower when you can use quantization and sustained batching — more like $0.10–0.25 per 1k tokens. Those are net compute estimates, don't forget to add storage/observability add-ons if needed.
03:05 Michael Torres: So just so I'm tracking, if our average call is ~950 tokens total, at say $0.5/1k that's about $0.48 per call? That math seems... high.
03:32 Priya Sharma: Right, it's easy to misread. At $0.5 per 1k tokens, 950 tokens ~= 0.95 * $0.5 = $0.475 per call. But with batching and KV caching we often reduce that by 40–70% for repeated prefixes in your flows. E.g., if you have standard intro text or system prompts cached, output tokens and some compute can be avoided.
04:10 Liam O'Connor: Curious about that caching — does Redwood do prefix caching only, or full KV retention between requests? We have multi-turn conversations where user context is often the same.
04:42 Priya Sharma: We have prefix/KV cache and can persist KV caches across requests on dedicated instances. On hosted, prefix cache is supported at the route level and gives you hit rates if your traffic is repetitive. On Dedicated you can do full KV warm starts, which is where you get the biggest delta. Small note: auto-generated docs might say 'KV cash' in transcripts though — sorry for the transcription typos.
05:15 Jordan Lee: On benchmarking approach: propose a 3-phase POC — baseline single-run on hosted to get raw latency & cost numbers, then dedicated pilot with quantized models and batching knobs, and finally a production-like run with prefix caching and workload-shaped QPS to estimate steady-state unit economics.
06:00 Michael Torres: Timeline? How long to get meaningful numbers?
06:15 Jordan Lee: We typically run an initial hosted benchmark in 1 week after we get traces and sample prompts. Dedicated pilot takes longer to provision — 2–3 weeks for instance provisioning and model tuning, then 1 week of steady-state runs. So end-to-end about 6–8 weeks.
07:05 Simone Park: What metrics will you capture in the runs? We'll need both latency percentiles and per-token compute costs.
07:30 Priya Sharma: We'll capture: per-request and per-token latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU utilization, tokens/sec, batching statistics (batch size distribution), KV cache hit rate, and cost per 1k tokens as broken down by model compute, GPU amortization, and infra overhead. Also will run regression accuracy checks against your eval set to ensure quantization doesn't degrade quality beyond your threshold.
08:10 Michael Torres: Good — our success criteria: p95 <= 200ms for short summaries; for long summaries we'd accept p95 <= 800ms, and cost target $0.20 or lower per user request on average. If we can hit those we can move to pilot.
09:00 Jordan Lee: Noted — we'll try to map your per-request cost target to per-1k-token numbers and what that implies for batching and quantization. Quick example we ran for a similar customer: nominal hosted cost was $0.60/1k tokens, but with dedicated + int8 quantization + optimal batching they got to $0.12/1k tokens, a ~80% reduction. But results are workload dependent.
09:45 Liam O'Connor: Any change in output quality with INT8 or Q4_0 quant? We cannot have hallucinations increase or summaries lose key facts.
10:10 Priya Sharma: We'll include the accuracy/regression suite in the POC. Typically small degradations can appear with aggressive quant, but sometimes tuning (per-layer quant thresholds) recovers most of the gap. We'll gate on your quality thresholds.
10:45 Terry Nguyen: About traffic shaping, can Redwood simulate the different mixes we talked about? Short vs long summary splits?
11:05 Priya Sharma: Yes, we'll provide a load generator and a runbook. We'll run separate scenarios: short-only, long-only, and mixed weighted by your real distribution. That will show sensitivity of per-token unit cost to request composition.
11:45 Jordan Lee: On pricing/practicalities: for the POC we can offer a time-limited dedicated pilot discount and credits for hosted runs. We'll send a POC pricing sheet with cost sensitivity rows — e.g., cost per 1k token at batch sizes 1/4/8/16, and with/without KV caching.
12:20 Michael Torres: For the benchmark itself, what do you need from us to start?
12:35 Jordan Lee: Three things: 1) anonymized request traces for 1 week (or recent logs), 2) 1000 sample prompts representing edge cases, and 3) confirmation on SLOs and quality thresholds. Also let us know if you want private deployment (VPC/on-prem) to be evaluated — that'll add provisioning time.
13:05 Michael Torres: We'll get the traces. We do want to evaluate private deployment, at least as a possibility, but route the initial benchmark on hosted to get baseline numbers.
13:30 Priya Sharma: Okay. A couple technical notes we discussed: for dedicated runs we'll probably test A100 80GB vs an M40 (or equivalent Ampere) depending on model size, and test quantized checkpoints e.g., fp16, int8, q4_0. Also measure batching windows — sometimes a 40ms batching window increases p95 slightly but halves per-token cost for many workloads.
14:05 Simone Park: Can we see a sample report from another POC? Even anonymized would help the execs.
14:20 Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include an anonymized benchmark report and a spreadsheet showing the cost model breakdown.
14:40 Liam O'Connor: What about security/compliance for the POC? We need SOC2 and SSO, and if we go private we need KMS integration.
15:00 Jordan Lee: We'll share our security pack — SOC2 cert, SAML/SSO integration guide, and options for KMS/HSM for private installs. That will be in the docs packet Priya will send.
15:30 Michael Torres: Back to economics — can you show an example per-request calc in the deck? It's easier to get buy-in if we see the math.
15:45 Jordan Lee: Absolutely. Example slide: average tokens per request * (cost per token) = cost per request. Then multiply by daily active users and conversions to estimate monthly cost. We'll include sensitivity for different batch sizes and cache hit rates.
16:10 Priya Sharma: And we'll add an ROI row showing cost per 1k tokens across hosts: baseline hosted, dedicated no quant, dedicated with int8, and dedicated with batching + cache.
16:35 Michael Torres: I also want to call out budget constraints — we have a pilot budget of $35k for the POC phase including any dedicated pilot hours. If the numbers require more, we'll need to see strong justification.
17:00 Jordan Lee: Understood — we'll structure the scope to fit that budget; often the hosted baseline and a short dedicated pilot can fit under that if we limit run hours and use off-peak scheduling. We'll show a best/worst case cost schedule.
17:30 Simone Park: One more question on observability — can we get token-level tracing and per-route cost details?
17:45 Priya Sharma: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakouts, per-route latency/cost, and tracing hooks you can forward to your observability platform. For the POC we'll enable a short retention with more detail.
18:10 Liam O'Connor: Regarding network setup for private pilot, we may need IP allowlists and a VPC peering agreement. I'll coordinate with our infra team after the meeting.
18:30 Jordan Lee: Great. To recap next steps quickly: Jordan send pricing + POC contract by 10/10; Priya send runbook and scripts by 10/09; Arcadia to share traces and sample prompts by 10/13; schedule kick-off wk of 10/20. Any objections?
19:05 Michael Torres: No objections, that works. Thanks everyone.
19:20 Jordan Lee: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet.

(Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' vs KV cache, 'M40' may be mis-attributed, speaker turns sometimes truncated.)
